summary: Well-executed, preregistered paired study that evaluates a verifier‑grounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline for intent→configuration NetOps tasks in a provenance‑traced Mininet emulation (N=200 paired intents, shared_initial_candidate). Execution artifacts appear complete and consistent with the preregistration; primary inferential test (exact McNemar) did not reject (p=0.125). The manuscript explicitly documents shared_initial_candidate semantics, the model configuration temperature=null caveat, and the mandatory master‑prompt provenance. No new experiments are requested, but a few focused manuscript edits are needed before finalisation.
required_revisions: Ensure the References section is a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography with full bibliographic metadata (authors, title, venue, year, DOI/identifier as metadata), not bare DOI/arXiv/identifier lines; update the compiled manuscript to reflect this formatting.

Add one explicit, unambiguous sentence in Methods that: under shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation was produced per intent and that this single sampled candidate was reused by both baseline and guarded conditions (state initial_generation_calls_per_task=1), and therefore any between‑condition differences within a pair can only arise from deterministic validation and the permitted repair call.

In Methods (analysis subsection) explicitly state that the paired bootstrap percentile interval is auxiliary/exploratory and not part of the preregistered confirmatory inference (which is the exact McNemar test); add a short sentence noting that resampling intervals may exclude zero in sparse‑discordant situations even when the preregistered exact test is non‑significant.
optional_revisions: Consider a brief caveat about the limitations of bootstrap intervals with very few discordant pairs (n10+n01 small) and why you nonetheless report the percentile CI as descriptive.
Condense the Disclosure Statement slightly to avoid repeating execution/log bookkeeping already archived (preserve the mandatory master_prompt path and SHA‑256 verbatim).
Add a small exemplar table or appendix paragraph describing the four baseline violation cases and the repair content/traces to aid readers' qualitative understanding of the corrected fault modes.
